input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "preservation",
 "diagnosis": "The bounds invariant `0 <= i <= a.Length + 1` is too weak: it admits i == a.Length + 1, so in the quantified invariant `forall k :: 0 <= k < i ==> b[k] == a[(a.Length-1) - k]` the index k can reach a.Length, making b[k] and a[(a.Length-1)-k] (= a[-1]) out of range. The invariant is therefore not well-formed in an arbitrary loop iteration state. Tightening the bound to `0 <= i <= a.Length` (which the body maintains since it only runs while i < a.Length) fixes well-formedness and also gives i == a.Length at exit for the postcondition."}
EOF
sed -i 's/invariant 0<=i<= (a.Length) + 1/invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length/' program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
`program.dfy` now verifies: Dafny reports 3 verified, 0 errors.

**Cause:** The loop's bounds invariant said `0 <= i <= a.Length + 1`. That allows `i == a.Length + 1`, and then the second invariant (`forall k :: 0 <= k < i ==> b[k] == a[(a.Length-1) - k]`) can use `k == a.Length`. At that value both `b[k]` and `a[-1]` are out of range, so the invariant isn't well-formed in an arbitrary loop state. Those are the two errors at line 27. I logged it in `diagnosis.json` as `invariant` / `preservation`.

**Fix (line 25):** I tightened the bound to `invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length`. The loop keeps this true because it only runs while `i < a.Length`. When the loop ends, `i == a.Length`, so the quantified invariant gives the postcondition directly.

I also removed the trailing semicolon after the `ensures` clause on line 17. Dafny flagged it as deprecated style, and with warnings not allowed it would have stopped compilation. It had no effect on verification.
